faqs.question: I see the message Ink Cartridge Error: Replace Ink Cartridge. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
An ink cartridge in your printer needs to be replaced. The cartridge may be expended, or the IC chip on the cartridge may not be communicating properly. Try reseating the cartridge and turning the printer off and on. If you still see the error message, try installing a different ink cartridge in the printer.
If this did not solve the problem, contact Epson support.

faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: I see the message No Ink Cartridge Install Ink Cartridge when all ink cartridges are installed. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The ink cartridge(s) you installed may not be recognized by the printer. Try reseating the ink cartridge(s) and turning the printer off and on. If you still see the error message, try installing a different ink cartridge in the printer.
If this did not solve the problem, contact Epson support.

faqs.question: I see the message Communication Error when I use a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Delete all print jobs in the print queue.
Turn the printer off.
Note:
Make sure the USB cable is connected correctly.
Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.question: Why do I need color ink cartridges when I print in black only?
faqs.answer:
The printer will not print if any ink cartridge is expended or removed. Epson printers contain a permanent print head that needs to be charged with all colors to work. Even when you are printing black text only, a small amount of color ink is used to keep the print head charged. The print head needs to be kept charged to prevent air bubbles from entering. Air bubbles can damage the print head.
Therefore, once one of the cartridges is expended, the printer signals you to replace the cartridge in order for printing to continue.

faqs.question: I see the message Service error 4000. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Turn off the printer, then turn it back on. Run a power cleaning cycle, then print a nozzle check pattern to make sure all the nozzles print. If this does not help, contact Epson support.

faqs.question: I see the message Maintenance error 0040. What does it indicate?
faqs.answer: The error code indicates the cleaning mechanism has reached its end of life. Contact Epson for further assistance.

faqs.question: I see a message that starts with DXXX. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Turn off the printer and disconnect all cables connected to the printer. Wait 30 seconds, connect the cables again, and turn on the printer. If this does not help, contact Epson support.

Note:

faqs.answer: No. The printer has mechanical ink valves that close when the printer is powered off.  For transportation, an ink cartridge (empty or full) should be installed in each ink slot.

faqs.question: How much ink is used during the switching of black ink modes?
faqs.answer:
The amount of ink used during the black ink switch is as follows:
Photo Black to Matte Black uses about 1.13ml (approx. 2:07 minutes)
Matte Black to Photo Black uses about 3.34ml (approx. 2:55 minutes)

faqs.question: Why are there 3 different sizes of ink cartridges available for my product?
faqs.answer: Ink cartridges are available in three sizes (150 ml, 350 ml, and 700 ml) to meet the demands of varying usage.

faqs.question: Do I need a black ink conversion kit to switch between photo black and matte black ink?
faqs.answer: No.  The printer can switch between inks quickly without an ink conversion kit.

faqs.question: Does my product have a pressurized ink delivery system?
faqs.answer: Yes. This ensures positive ink flow even when the printer is used at higher elevations or if the floor is not completely level.

faqs.question: How many prints can I print from an ink cartridge in my printer?
faqs.answer: There are too many variables to provide a count. You can estimate the amount by printing a Job Information sheet from the printer's Test Print menu. This sheet provides the amount of ink used for the last 10 print jobs, which can help you calculate ink usage.

faqs.question: My printer's ink cartridges are half full after I install the first set of ink cartridges. Why does this happen?
faqs.answer: Ink from the first set of ink cartridges is used to charge the printer's ink delivery system. This will not happen again when you install new ink cartridges.

faqs.question: Can I use an expired ink cartridge in my printer?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend using expired ink cartridges in the printer. Do not use an unopened ink cartridge if the date on the package has expired. For best results, use ink cartridges before the expiration date printed on the package (and within six months of installation in the printer). Replace expired cartridges with new ones.
You may need to replace a cartridge that is more than six months old, if your printouts do not look their best, even after cleaning and aligning the printhead. We recommend you store any unused or unopened ink cartridges in a cool, dark place.

faqs.question: I see the message Ink Cartridge Error: Replace Ink Cartridge. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
An ink cartridge in your printer needs to be replaced. The cartridge may be expended, or the IC chip on the cartridge may not be communicating properly. Try reseating the cartridge and turning the printer off and on. If you still see the error message, try installing a different ink cartridge in the printer.
If this did not solve the problem, contact Epson support.

faqs.question: I can tell some ink is still in the ink cartridge. Why does my printer show that the cartridge is expended?
faqs.answer: The ink cartridge is designed to include a small safety reserve of ink. This safety reserve prevents damage to the printhead. If the printer tries to print when no ink remains in the cartridge, air bubbles would enter the ink delivery system and cause damage to the permanent printhead. The safety reserve of ink prevents this from happening.

faqs.answer:
The ink cartridge(s) you installed may not be recognized by the printer. Try reseating the ink cartridge(s) and turning the printer off and on. If you still see the error message, try installing a different ink cartridge in the printer.

Air bubbles can damage the print head.
Therefore, once one of the cartridges is expended, the printer signals you to replace the cartridge in order for printing to continue.

Make sure High Speed is not selected.
Lower the dpi setting you selected to print.  If you selected 2880 dpi, lower                     the setting to 1440 dpi.
Make sure the lines are not in the image source.
Make sure you use the correct profile settings.

Horizontal Banding

faqs.question: Why are only matte media types displayed in the driver's media list?
faqs.answer: When matte black ink is selected in the printer driver, only matte media types are displayed in the driver list.  The complete media list appears only when the photo black ink is selected.

faqs.question: Why should I use the Matte Black mode?
faqs.answer: The standard Photo Black ink has been optimized for resin coated (RC) and Photographic grade media types. If you're printing on matte-type papers such as Epson Velvet Fine Art, Enhanced Matte, or UltraSmooth Fine Art, the black density will be significantly better if you use Matte Black ink.

faqs.question: What does the LFP Remote Panel Utility do?
faqs.answer:
This utility provides an easy way to:
Update firmware
Perform nozzle checks
Run the bi-d and uni-d alignments/auto alignments
Print status sheets
Make custom paper settings
Perform power cleanings
Set the printer clock
Set media counter settings
Make paper feed adjustment
Monitor the printer using print watcher

faqs.question: What does the Common Updater 7.0 file do?
faqs.answer: The Common Updater 7.0 file provides the latest Mac OS X 10.6 support for your printer driver. Before installing the updater, make sure the most current version of the Mac OS X 10.5 or 10.6 printer driver is installed on your computer. Restart your computer after installing the updater.

faqs.question: What does the Optimize Enlargement option in my product driver do?
faqs.answer:
Select
Optimize Enlargement
if you are enlarging an image beyond the limits of your application program. The driver will increase the image size up to 650% and decrease the output resolution to stay within the pixel limitations. Depending on the resolution of the original image and the print size, you may see reduced quality in the print.

faqs.question: Which interfaces does my product support?
faqs.answer: The printer supports USB 2.0 and Ethernet 10/100 connections.

faqs.question: When should I use the product profiles that end in PK and MK?
faqs.answer: Use the profile that ends in PK when photo black ink is selected on the printer. Use the profile that ends in MK when matte black ink is selected on the printer.

faqs.question: The Advanced B&W Photo setting is grayed out in my product driver. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The Advanced B&W setting is dependent on which black ink cartridge is selected.  When the photo black ink cartridge is selected, the Advanced B&W function is available only for glossy media types.  When the matte black ink cartridge is selected, the Advanced B&W function is available only for matte media types.

faqs.question: Does Epson offer RIP software for my product?
faqs.answer: Epson does not currently offer any RIP software for this printer.

faqs.question: What is the Epson Advanced Black & White Printing Mode?
faqs.answer: This is a proprietary Epson screening and color management technology designed specifically to produce professional-level black and white prints. This unique screen technology takes advantage of our three-level black technology—along with Yellow, Light Cyan, and Vivid Light Magenta—to produce professional black and white prints from either color or grayscale files. Epson's new Advanced Black & White printing technology is simply another tool for achieving the ultimate black and white print.

faqs.question: What is the High Speed setting in the Epson driver?
faqs.answer:
When
High Speed
is selected, the print head prints in both directions (bi-directional) to speed up printing. When
High Speed
is deselected or turned off, the printer prints in one direction (uni-directional) only, which produces the highest quality images, but slows down printing.

faqs.question: How do Media Counter Settings work?
faqs.answer:
To access the Media Counter Settings you must first launch the Epson LFP Remote Panel Utility. The Media Counter Settings allow you to select when low paper messages will appear on the printer's control panel, based on the quantity of remaining media. If another print job is sent to the printer while the
Paper Low
message is displayed, the status monitor will display an alert and ask whether to continue or cancel the print.
When alternating between different rolls, it is essential to keep track of what roll is being used in the printer. To clear an alert, load a new roll or a sheet of paper in the printer and set the parameters. Turning off the media counter also clears the alert on the control panel.
Note:
Only roll paper media can be counted.

faqs.question: Do I need a raster image processor (RIP) to print from Adobe Illustrator?
faqs.answer:
For the best output, a RIP should be used. Adobe Illustrator is a postscript application that requires a RIP to translate the postscript language. The printer comes with a non-postscript driver that has difficulty translating the postscript language.
Epson has partnered with the following manufacturers for some printers:
ColorBurst
efi
Onyx
Wasatch

faqs.question: Do I need a raster image processor (RIP) to print from Adobe Photoshop?
faqs.answer: No, Adobe Photoshop is not a postscript application and does not require a RIP.

faqs.question: How do I save my Epson printer driver presets so I can restore them if I reinstall the Epson printer driver in Windows?
faqs.answer:
Note:
You may lose some custom settings when you uninstall the printer driver.
Before you reinstall the printer driver, do the following:
Open
File Explorer
or
Windows Explorer
.
Select
This PC
or
Computer
>
C:
drive >
Program Files
>
Epson
> [your printer name].
Move the UCI extension files to a different folder on your desktop.
Note:
After you reinstall the Epson printer driver, move the UCI extension files back to your printer's folder as described in step 2.

faqs.question: How do I install the ICC profiles in Windows XP or Windows 7?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Download the ICC profiles for your printer and save them in a folder you can easily find.
Close all open software.
Open
Windows Explorer
, then select
Computer
>
C:
drive >
Windows
>
System32
>
spool
>
drivers
>
color
.
Move the ICC profiles into the
color
folder, then close all open windows.

faqs.question: How do I manually install the Epson ICC profiles on my Mac?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Open your hard drive, then select
Library
>
Printers
>
EPSON
>
InkjetPrinters2
>
ICCProfiles
.
Press and hold the
control
key on your keyboard while you select
Show Package Contents
.
Select
Contents
>
Resources
, select and copy all files, then close all open windows.
Open your hard drive, select
Library
>
ColorSync
>
Profiles
, then paste the files into this folder.

faqs.question: Where are the ICC profiles located for my printer on my Mac?
faqs.answer:
Do the following to locate the files:
Open your hard drive, then select
Library
>
Printers
>
EPSON
>
InkjetPrinter2
>
ICCProfiles
.
Press and hold the
Control
key on your keyboard while you click the profile package in the
ICCProfiles
folder. In the pop-up menu that appears, select
Show Package Contents
.
Select
Contents
>
Resources

faqs.question: What is the minimum page size supported by my product?
faqs.answer: The minimum page size is 8.27 inches x 11 inches.

faqs.question: Which connection enables my product to operate at full speed?
faqs.answer: Both built-in USB (USB port on the computer must be 2.0 compatible) and Ethernet connections allow the printer to operate at full print engine speed. Your CPU is the biggest factor in print engine speed.

faqs.question: What is the maximum resolution for printing?

faqs.answer:

faqs.question: Does my product stand come with my product?
faqs.answer: Yes.

faqs.question: What are my product's features?
faqs.answer:
The Epson Stylus Pro 9900 offers the following features:
New Vivid Magenta and Vivid Light Magenta inks for more vibrant color
Advanced MicroPiezo TFP print head with ink-repelling coating technology
10-channel, drop-on-demand, ink jet print head
11-cartridge (orange, green, cyan, light cyan, vivid magenta, vivid light magenta, yellow, light black, light light black, photo black or matte black) ink system
Auto head alignment and cleaning technology
Auto sharing black ink channel (photo black and matte black)
Epson UltraChrome HDR ink technology
44-inch roll and manual feed capability
Printer stand
Built-in media cutter
Improved resolution of 2880 x 1440 dpi
Three cartridge fill volumes available:  150ml, 350ml, or 700ml
Two user-replaceable maintenance tanks
Borderless printing capability on various media
Fast print speed
On-demand ink valve damper
Icon-based printer control panel with back-lit LCD
Remote Panel Utility for performing firmware updates, custom paper configuration, and print head alignment
Epson driver supports custom paper configuration, auto nozzle check, and print head cleaning
Standard built-in USB and EtherNet interfaces
Epson PreciseColor Technology
UltraChrome HDR Ink light fastness: color up to 200 years; B&W over 200 years
Note
: Ink lightfastness rating based on accelerated testing of prints on specialty media, displayed indoors, under glass.  Actual print stability will vary according to media, printed image, display conditions, light intensity, humidity, and atmospheric conditions. Epson does not guarantee longevity of prints.  For maximum print life, display all print under glass or lamination, or store them properly.

faqs.question: How many nozzles does my product use for each color?
faqs.answer: The printer uses 360 nozzles per color.

faqs.question: Is an extended warranty available for my product?
faqs.answer:

Options and Accessories

faqs.question: How do I get service for my product I purchased in another country?
faqs.answer: Due to differences in products sold in other countries, printers need to be serviced in the country of origin.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
